title: Smoother startup and dungeon cameras
summary: Added an immediate loading screen, reduced dungeon camera overhead, and removed the unfinished explorable World Atlas.
changes: The loading message now appears immediately while the game downloads, instead of a blank green screen.
Camera collision checks now avoid scanning every stone triangle each frame. Walls, openings and overhead arches keep their existing camera collision, appearance and movement rules.
Removed the unfinished explorable World Atlas. The M map and minimap remain available. Characters last saved in the atlas return to their previous location in the main world.

title: Start a fresh dungeon after clearing it
summary: Leaving a completed dungeon no longer keeps you stuck in the cleared run because completion rewards were left unclaimed.
changes: After everyone deliberately leaves a completed run, entering again starts a fresh dungeon. Party members who have finished leaving are told to wait for the remaining adventurers instead of being sent back into cleared rooms.
Unclaimed completion rewards follow you out as personal loot beside the entrance for five minutes, keeping the same items and any partial claims. Ordinary boss and cache loot stays in the dungeon.
Disconnect recovery still preserves the existing run for ten minutes after its last member leaves.

title: Reduce movement snap-back after server lag
summary: Recently moving adventurers can catch up after a brief realm stall without being pulled back for otherwise valid movement.
changes: Walking, sprinting and riding now account for a brief delay measured on the server when processing movement already in flight. Movement speed, stamina, collisions and blocked routes remain authoritative. Idle time and client-reported timing cannot provide extra movement allowance.

title: Reduce overworld server delays
summary: Reduced unnecessary work when preparing world updates for adventurers in the overworld.
changes: The realm now skips terrain-height checks for monsters and resources that are already too far away to appear in your world update. Nearby visibility, height checks and dungeon updates stay the same.

title: Repair interrupted game updates
summary: Fixed automatic updates getting stuck after the arena wallet configuration changed.
changes: Automatic updates now accept the arena wallet settings and can reuse verified downloads from the failed update. The previous complete game remains available until the replacement is ready.
Restored verified treasury payout and balance figures on the public statistics page when the network provider cannot look up older block headers by number.

title: More reliable realm entry during busy reconnects
summary: Reduced connection timeouts when several adventurers sign in or change realms together.
changes: Reduced unnecessary waits while loading accounts, helping simultaneous sign-ins and realm changes finish before the connection times out. Account ownership, deletion safeguards and saved progress remain protected.

title: Keep other adventurers aligned with terrain steps
summary: Grounded adventurers no longer briefly hover while walking up or down terrain steps.
changes: Fixed other players briefly appearing above or inside ordinary terrain steps while walking. Their feet now follow the terrain at their displayed position.

title: Move freely after returning to a dungeon checkpoint
summary: Sanctuary checkpoints no longer trap returning adventurers inside their floating markers.
changes: Fixed players being unable to move after resuming a dungeon, respawning or recovering from a party wipe at an activated sanctuary checkpoint, including Veilhaven Monastery.
Checkpoint glyphs and rings are passable. Dungeon floors, walls, chests and other solid scenery keep their collision.

title: Clearer reward and wallet reviews
summary: See expedition rewards and recognized MOSS arena transaction terms before continuing.
changes: Treasure-map journals show Gold, potions, ancient coins and the voucher chance together above the expedition action. Rewards remain reserved for the map owner.
Recognized MOSS arena wallet requests show the stake, opponent, pot, tax and refund deadlines. Unrecognized transactions keep their full transaction review.

title: A complete interface, on desktop and mobile
summary: Clearer game windows and touch controls in Mossvale’s familiar forest and gold style.
changes: Story quests now have an active/completed list, a detailed objective sheet, live progress and reward details. Track an objective to pin it to the HUD; ready quests show a route back to their giver.
The desktop HUD separates a centered ability bar from a compact menu dock. Paused specialist XP stays out of the HUD. Saved HUD size settings remain available.
Backpack opens directly to your bags, with item search, capacity tabs and grid/list views. Filtering does not move or change your items.
Trainer filters show counts for available, upcoming and learned abilities. Merchant and trainer details sit beside the list on desktop and beneath the selected row on phones.
Touch controls now place five skills around Attack, with four pages for your twenty slots. A compact quest tracker stays visible, and Menu opens a full-screen grid with labelled buttons.
Bank shows your bags beside stored items on desktop, with search and sorting. Auction item details follow the selected row on phones, and the NFT collection separates houses, pets and mounts.

Spellbook search includes learned and upcoming abilities. Mobile Skill Tree branches, workshop progression, collection filters, friend groups and achievement progress make larger catalogs easier to browse.

Arena highlights your highest bracket and next rank. Dungeons, Instant Combat and raids show their requirements, stages and rewards more clearly. Sign-in, loading and wallet pages keep the existing secure actions and Mossvale artwork.

title: Read chat in your language
summary: Choose a chat language on realms with translation enabled.
changes: Chat now has an optional language picker for Google Translate, with 24 languages and a preference saved on this device.

World, party and incoming whisper messages can be translated automatically. Select Original beside a translated message to read what the player wrote; sending and reporting messages keep the original text.
Translation is off by default and requires the realm to enable it. If translation is unavailable or its limit is reached, original messages remain readable.

title: Lower data usage while playing and loading
summary: Smaller world downloads and more efficient game updates reduce data usage.
changes: World updates use stronger compression and reuse repeated data on supported connections, with the same update frequency.
Your connection receives your own personal loot drops, reducing background data from other players’ uncollected loot.
World collision downloads now use lossless compression, reducing the data needed when loading uncached areas.
The browser reuses verified files it just loaded when saving the game for your next visit, avoiding a second background download of those files.
Friends and Achievements header artwork loads when you open those panels instead of during startup.

title: Lighter background wallet checks
summary: Verified empty NFT wallets use fewer background chain requests.
changes: After all NFT collections verify that a linked wallet is empty, automatic ownership checks run about once a minute. Open Pets & Mounts to refresh immediately after receiving your first NFT.
Wallets holding NFT pets, mounts or house deeds keep their frequent ownership checks. Transferred-away collectibles still lose access, and minting and payment verification keep their existing checks.

title: Reduced collision memory growth
summary: Lower memory pressure as players travel across the world and visit dungeon instances.
changes: Collision data shares one cache limit across overworld and dungeon areas. Older cached areas release their memory for reuse before new areas are loaded, reducing server memory pressure while keeping solid collision active.
Reduced server work when adventurers are spread across the world by skipping unnecessary monster detection checks for distant players. Aggro ranges and safe areas are unchanged.

title: Automatic steps across terrain
summary: Moving across ordinary terrain rises lifts your character onto the next tile again.
changes: Moving across overworld terrain automatically lifts you onto ordinary rises of up to 1.5 meters.
Solid scenery, walls and ceilings retain their collision. Climbing remains disabled.

title: Climbing removed, solid surfaces retained
summary: Run around scenery without grabbing it, while keeping physical walls, floors and supported tops.
changes: Climbing is disabled. Moving into portals, chests, walls or other scenery no longer starts a climb or drains climbing stamina.
Solid objects still block movement. Walking, jumping, small steps, ceilings and standing on supported surfaces remain in place.

title: Smoother walking around solid scenery
summary: Move around obstacles and step away from an opening chest while keeping solid surfaces.
changes: When running past a portal, chest or other solid object, walking tries to slide around it.
Opening a chest beside your character no longer traps you against its moving lid. You can walk back out while the chest stays solid.

title: Reduced collision stalls
summary: Smaller collision areas reduce pauses while moving around detailed scenery and when players are spread across the world.
changes: Reduced pauses near detailed scenery and when players are spread across towns. Solid surfaces, open doorways and ceilings retain their collision behavior.

title: Explore the World Atlas
summary: An additional world of 39 connected maps, with six realm routes and saved travel.
changes: Open the map while in a town and choose Explore the World Atlas. Your character, equipment and existing progress travel with you; return from the Lanternreach arrival point.
Walk through map gates or interact with realm doors to travel. Each map has its own terrain, collision, map markers and shared multiplayer space. Reconnecting resumes your atlas location.
The atlas currently supports exploration. Its shops, quests, monster encounters and SP trials are not yet available; the existing world remains available for these activities.

title: Stories and chambers along the road
summary: 82 one-time quests, six story chambers and clearer windows in Mossvale’s established style.
changes: Mossvale keeps its original forest, parchment and gold frames and lettering. Merchant and trainer lists share a window with item details; mobile controls and story actions remain usable.

82 non-specialist story quests add NPC dialogue with accept/decline choices, ordered objectives, 54 placed objects, 40 named or area-specific enemy spawns, and two personal rescue or escort encounters. The journal can track story objects and chamber entrances.

Six quest chambers unlock at levels 7, 10, 14, 18, 24 and 44. Follow their seals, keys and mechanisms in order. Three timed wave encounters last thirty seconds; protect the Hollow Door lantern from inside its six-meter circle.

Return to the quest giver for one-time XP, materials, profession XP or gear. Select a reward when a weapon or armor choice is offered. Story chambers have no repeatable completion chest or leaderboard. The required Ashbound and optional Sun chamber treasures each grant one ancient coin per character.
Heatproofing awards a Heatproof tonic. Drink it for 20% less fire damage for five minutes, with the shared ten-second consumable cooldown. Another tonic refreshes the duration without stacking.

Matching supplied loot and resource artwork and optional UI sounds support existing game actions. NPC services still require visiting their locations; quest rewards and purchases remain controlled by the realm.

title: Boss combat and weapon artwork
summary: Distinct Instant Combat skills, updated Apostle animations and Epic/Mythic weapon art.
changes: The eight Instant Combat bosses each use three distinct skills with authoritative ground warnings, stacking/spreading, rescue targets, tank swaps and status effects. Their existing 70% and 35% shield objectives remain.
The Horned Apostle uses updated forms and spell effects, with separate emergence, transition, sustained channel and final-enrage animations.
Epic and Mythic weapons use class-specific animated artwork at their base and +5 stages. Equipment upgrades still stop at +5, with item stats and drop rates retained.
Specialist upgrade visuals now show the channel and saved success, unchanged or fracture result on your current character.

title: Specialist classes paused
summary: Current SP classes are disabled while owned cards and progression are preserved.
changes: Specialist cards cannot be equipped and no longer grant combat power, defense, specialist wings or Job XP. Previously equipped cards are also inactive.
Cards, saved Job XP, upgrade ranks and NFT ownership are retained. Claiming, upgrading, repairing and trading cards remain available. Apostle cosmetic wings and base classes are unchanged.
The current realm keeps its level-60 cap.

title: Climb and stand on solid scenery
summary: Climb terrain and solid scenery using stamina, with physical surfaces and climbing animations for every playable character model.
changes: Hold movement toward a solid surface while on foot to climb, using the keyboard or touch joystick. Climb onto rocks, trees, buildings, walls and other scenery, stand on their tops, and jump or fall off. Doorways remain open and ceilings stop jumps. Dungeon portals and match boundaries still control access.

Climbing drains the existing stamina bar at 20 energy per second and stops stamina recovery. Running out of energy makes you drop; recover to 25 before climbing again. The realm controls climbing height, movement and energy use.
All nine races, both body variants and all four classes use a Blender-authored climbing cycle. Weapons and tools are tucked away while climbing, and nearby players see the same climbing state.

title: Smaller chat with its own size control
summary: Desktop chat is more compact and can be resized independently from the hotbar and menu.
changes: Desktop chat defaults to 80% size. Adjust Chat size from 60% to 125% in Settings → Graphics without changing the hotbar or menu.
Your chat size is saved on this device. Reset restores 80%; the chat window still supports mouse and keyboard resizing, channel tabs and scrolling.
Changing chat size preserves your reading position. Mobile chat keeps its existing layout.

title: Pet drops require level 10 monsters
summary: Slimes and monsters below level 10 no longer drop pets.
changes: Pets can drop only from their eligible source monsters at level 10 or higher. Slimes cannot drop pets at any level.
Clover Mouse no longer drops. Existing pets stay available to their owners; unlearned copies remain usable and tradable.

title: Updated spells and talent trees
summary: New passives, revised spell tuning and resurrection for Clerics.
changes: All four classes use the updated 137-spell and 130-talent catalogues, with twenty new spell and talent icons. The downloadable workshops contain the same playable settings and artwork.

Rangers gain Precise Shots, Primal Focus and Natural Gift. Mages gain Heated Haste, Magic Focus and Sharp Mind. Updated Knight and Cleric passives grant critical chance, total damage, maximum health, healing pulses and timed defense as described in their trees.

Ricochet Shot makes five impacts and can hit an enemy repeatedly, retaining 85% damage on each repeat against that target. Adamant Guardian reduces damage by 40% and immediately counterattacks at most once per second. Hold the Line adds 5% or 10% of absorbed damage to its reflection.

Clerics can use Revivify to return nearby fallen group allies to full health in place. It is instant with no spell cooldown, follows the normal global cooldown, requires a clear path and cannot restore eliminated arena fighters.

Updated healing, shield and attack spell timings and strength match the revised class catalogue. Retired spells are removed from spellbooks and their hotbar slots without resetting other assignments. Compatible talent builds remain allocated; valid builds whose prerequisites changed receive their points back.

title: Spellbook, raid and input recovery fixes
summary: More reliable spell selection, raid controls, mobile input and audio recovery.
changes: Spell details now have their own space below the spell lists, keeping every skill selectable.
Leaving a raid while dead restores the normal revive prompt. Live raid updates preserve expanded guides, invite controls, focus and scroll position.
Mobile movement stops when a touch ends outside the joystick or the device rotates, with independent handling for the other thumb.
A new user interaction can retry audio recovery even when the browser left an earlier resume request pending.
Active shields show their remaining absorption and time. Blessed Armor and Adamant Guardian also show their active effects.
Overworld enemies use obstacle detours around trees and rocks while retaining collision, movement-speed and safe-area restrictions.

title: A smaller desktop HUD with adjustable size
summary: The desktop hotbar, XP bars and connected menu start 60% smaller.
changes: The joined desktop HUD defaults to 40% of its previous size, leaving more of the world visible.
Adjust Hotbar size in Settings → Graphics from 30% to 100%. The hotbar, XP bars and connected menu resize together immediately, and your choice is saved on this device. Reset restores 40%.
Chat stays readable at its existing text size. Mobile and touch controls keep their existing size and layout.

title: Auction item details keep your place
summary: Live market updates no longer reset the selected item's scrollbar.
changes: Scroll through an auction item's stats without jumping back to the top when listings refresh.
Selecting a different listing starts its item details at the top.

title: A joined woodland desktop HUD
summary: The desktop action bar and menu now share the proportions of the woodland HUD artwork.
changes: Desktop chat sits above a wide action bar with forest-green backgrounds, cyan character XP, gold specialist Job XP, ten larger ability slots and two stacked bank buttons.
The menu rises from the right end of the action bar in a four-by-four grid. Its arrow collapses the menu; account and game-master controls remain accessible beside it.
Mobile and touch controls keep their existing layout.

title: Required mobile app updates at startup
summary: Mobile startup can require an available app update before entering Mossvale. Activation is separate for each store.
changes: Outdated mobile apps show an Update required screen with App Store or Google Play and Check again actions. There is no Skip option; TestFlight installations update through TestFlight.
The native startup check runs before opening the game, with a matching sign-in check for older installed apps loading the updated website. Supported versions and browser players continue normally.

Returning from the store rechecks while the native update screen is open. Connection failures keep the game blocked and offer retry. Required versions stay disabled until the matching store releases are available and the policy is activated.

title: Instant Combat attacks pierce more defense each round
summary: Creature attacks ignore a growing share of defense as the event advances.
changes: Instant Combat creatures bypass 30%, 40%, 50%, 60% and 70% of defense in rounds 1 through 5, including the creature groups before the final boss.
The bypass applies to normal and special creature attacks against players and combat companions. Boss ground warnings and failed mechanics retain their existing health-based damage.
Defense still protects you, so heavily armored characters can still take minimum damage from a weak early attack. World monsters and PvP keep their existing defense rules.

title: More visible mobile alerts and daily return reminders
summary: Push delivery is enabled for supported mobile apps, with more frequent event and invitation alerts. A new app build and device permission are required.
changes: A one-time prompt offers Enable events & invites, Add daily reminders too or Not now. Device permission is requested only after you choose to enable alerts. Your saved choices, including opt-outs, are remembered on this device across sign-outs.

Settings → Notifications lets you change World events, Invites and Come back to Mossvale separately. Events and invites are suggested for a first setup; daily return reminders are optional. Android alerts use prominent banners, sound and vibration when device settings allow.

Instant Combat signup alerts take priority over nearby world-boss alerts. Other world events are limited to one every five minutes per device, and invitations to one every ten seconds. Existing invitation eligibility and expiry rules still apply.

Optional return reminders begin after 24 hours away, then arrive at most once per day. Playing on any realm resets the absence. Notifications are suppressed while the app is open, and tapping one resumes the game.

title: Three enemy groups per round and ten-slot ability banks
summary: More enemies in Instant Combat, faster pressure and a centered action bar.
changes: Each Instant Combat round now has three successive enemy groups. The fifth round ends with the rotating boss after two creature groups. The existing 30-minute time limit remains.
Instant Combat monsters move twice as fast and attack 25% faster. Boss warning times remain readable, and each boss keeps its required mechanics.
All eight event bosses now have distinct attack and ritual animations, timed to their ground warnings and impacts.

Personal rewards are active after all three groups in each round are defeated. Surviving players have 20 seconds to collect their pickup, or 30 seconds after the boss. Individual monsters still drop no loot or XP.
Each desktop ability bank now has ten slots, with keys 1–9 and 0. Existing assignments stay in their original bank. Touch controls offer five pages of four slots.
The action bar is centered, and Hide/Menu at the bottom right collapses or restores the side menu.

title: A woodland action bar and chat in the world
summary: A clearer bottom HUD, conversation above your abilities, and speech bubbles over nearby adventurers.
changes: The desktop action bar has a leafy frame, cyan character XP and gold specialist Job XP, two selectable banks, and a compact menu grid. Existing ability assignments and touch controls are preserved.
Recent messages appear as colored channel and player lines above the HUD. Open chat to read history or type without opening a separate modal or hiding touch combat controls.
World messages appear briefly in a speech bubble above nearby players. Whispers and party messages stay in their own chat channels.
Friends and Who lists stay still during a touch gesture, so incoming updates cannot move a different request under the Accept button.
Update downloads bypass stale browser HTTP cache entries while retaining already verified files from interrupted downloads.

title: Game update download repair
summary: Game updates can finish downloading the latest arena and HUD artwork.
changes: Fixed an image delivery problem that prevented the latest game update from installing and left players on an older version.

title: Instant Combat wave rewards and arena fixes
summary: Survive escalating waves, collect personal timed rewards, and join events even while a game panel is open.
changes: Waves begin gently, build pressure in Wave 3 and become denser and more dangerous in Wave 4 before the final boss. Difficulty stays based on the starting group, so losses matter in later rounds.

Clearing a wave creates personal Gold and supply pickups for surviving participants. Collect within twenty seconds after Waves 1–4 and thirty seconds after the boss. Unclaimed pickups expire; other players cannot take yours. Individual enemies still grant no kill XP or ordinary drops.

Total Gold across all five pickups is 100, 200 or 300 for levels 16–30, 31–45 or 46–60. Early waves provide potions; later waves add Greater Tonics and crafting materials. The final pickup includes crystals, relics and a 20% Rare-or-better equipment roll. The boss clear also grants 600, 1,200 or 1,800 XP by bracket, following normal specialist progression and XP boosts.
Instant Combat monsters continually attack the closest living adventurer and pursue across the arena. Players can jump over low obstacles on both maps; tall scenery and the boundary remain solid.
Event invitations remain visible and usable above open game panels, including GM-triggered signups. Long chat messages stay inside the scrolling history without covering the input area.
Interrupted updates retain verified downloaded files for the next attempt. Stalled downloads time out and retry while the last complete version stays available.

title: Forest frames and a compact game menu
summary: The game panels follow the supplied forest artwork more closely, with aligned chat tabs and a smaller game menu.
changes: World, System, Whispers and Party now use matching live tabs, with a clear selected border that stays aligned when chat is resized.
The game menu uses a compact icon grid, including Store and Arena, with keyboard hints and a separate labelled touch menu. Chat tabs and Back also fit the narrowest phone screens.
Friends, Referral Rewards and the Adventure Board use matching gold controls and clearer reward sections. Referral progress, payouts and quest rewards continue to show live game values.

The spellbook has framed collections of skills to learn and learned abilities, with selected skill details and hotbar editing below. Inventory equipment and bag tabs use the matching emerald frames, and the character preview uses a woodland backdrop.

The Adventure Board has working Active, Noticeboard and Completed tabs. Open a contract for its own objective, progress and rewards view, then track its destination or return to the board. Existing acceptance, claim and cancellation rules remain unchanged.

The player HUD uses the supplied portrait, name and title frames with live green health and blue casting bars. Referral Rewards uses its compact lantern-and-banner layout, and desktop chat has a labelled Hide and Show control.

title: Scheduled Instant Combat arenas
summary: Register from anywhere for five rounds of cooperative combat in your level bracket.
changes: Instant Combat runs every two hours on each realm, starting at 00:00, 02:00 and every even hour UTC. A server warning and a compact arena-art invitation open registration five minutes before each start. The invitation shows the map, boss, bracket and countdown, with Join Event and Decline buttons. Decline dismisses this event; you can still register or withdraw through the Instant Combat menu before signup closes.

At registration close, eligible entrants are assigned by their current level: 16–30, 31–45 or 46–60. Each private arena holds up to twenty players; larger brackets split into additional arenas. Your group gets ninety seconds to prepare before the first of five combat rounds, with ten-second breaks between rounds.
Instant Combat is available from level 16. Characters below level 16 do not receive the join invitation and cannot register.

Be alive and finish any duel, arena match or pending save before entry. Registration is available from anywhere; accepted entrants return through their current activity’s safe exit before moving to the event. No late entries or rejoins are allowed. Leaving, dying or disconnecting ends your participation and returns you to the world; belongings are retained.
Bone Pit and Void Rift use their authored arena maps and new themed monsters. Each map rotates through four final bosses, with the same map and boss assigned to every arena in a scheduled event.
Targeted spells use each arena’s full playable boundaries, including its outer edges.

Four creature waves lead to the selected boss. Each boss has its own shielded mechanic at 70% and 35% health: breaking chains, soaking stomps, following musical notes, clearing broods, sealing rifts, escaping webs, baiting charges or turning away from a gaze. Complete each shielded mechanic before its countdown ends, with a harder version at the second health gate and extra charge travel time when needed. Read the boss attack shapes and move clear before they strike.
Game masters can open Realm events in the GM menu and start an extra five-minute Instant Combat signup. Players join voluntarily, and the regular two-hour UTC schedule stays unchanged.
Event teammates can heal and support one another without joining a four-player party. Event XP, gold and collectible rewards are not available yet.

title: Smoother scrolling in bags and auctions
summary: Touch scrolling stays steady through background updates, with fewer accidental item actions.
changes: Background updates to bags and Auction House lists wait for an active swipe to finish before redrawing, and unchanged bag contents keep their scrolling elements through ordinary game updates.
Touch controls distinguish a completed tap from a scrolling gesture. Scrolling through item lists and wallet settings no longer triggers an action when the touched control has moved with the list.

title: Dungeon recovery, safer purchases and item locks
summary: Keep dungeon progress after a disconnect, understand pending payments, protect valuable items and use less gameplay data.
changes: Defeating the final dungeon boss now opens the completion results and return portal even when boss adds or optional side rooms remain. Completion rewards are still awarded once.

An unfinished run stays available on the same realm for ten minutes after its last adventurer leaves. Original participants can return through its entrance to the reached checkpoint without repeating cleared rooms. Disconnect recovery also preserves unclaimed completion rolls during that grace period. Realm restarts still end these temporary runs.

Auction purchases now distinguish reservation, wallet review, submission and uncertain payment states. Payment evidence takes precedence over an expired payment window. Proven failures before transaction submission can be retried; uncertain submitted requests stay protected from duplicate payment.

Lock items from the backpack or bank to prevent accidental selling, dropping, auction listing or player trade. Locks follow bank transfers and equipment upgrades. Stack locks protect every unit of that item type; normal use and crafting remain available.
Ongoing world updates now use WebSocket compression where supported, reducing gameplay network traffic without lowering the update rate. Initial artwork downloads are separate.

title: Five referral reward tiers
summary: Qualified invitations now unlock five levels of MOSS Auction House rewards.
changes: Referrers now earn 0.10%, 0.25%, 0.50%, 0.75% and 1.00% of their qualified referrals’ later eligible MOSS purchase volume at 1, 10, 25, 50 and 100 qualified referrals. The Wayfinder Sprite and Wayfarer Stag still unlock at ten and twenty-five.

The total MOSS seller fee remains 5%. Treasury and developer each receive 1.25% of the purchase price; the remaining 2.50% burns before referral rewards. Rewards reduce only burning, down to 1.50% at the highest tier. Sellers still receive 95%, and buyers pay the listed price.
Existing listings carry over. Already-signed payments keep their original contract and fee terms, and previous MOSS proceeds remain collectible from their original contracts.

title: Prepare referral settlement continuity
summary: Keep Auction House payments and proceeds recoverable during the referral contract rollout.
changes: Added support for the next referral settlement contract while keeping the current contract active for new purchases. Existing orders retain their signed terms, and proceeds remain collectible from the contract that earned them.

title: New menu icons and forest UI layouts
summary: Updated navigation artwork and clearer spell, inventory, social and adventure panels.
changes: The game menu now uses the new illustrated icons for bags, quests, character gear, combat skills, talents, crafting, Arena, achievements, Friends, Referrals, pets, Store, NFTs, settings and account. Wallet and Specialist panels use their matching icons.
Friends and Referral Rewards use forest-and-gold frames, clearer rows and visible progress. Referral amounts continue to follow the active contract schedule.

The spellbook separates skills to learn from learned abilities, shows selected ability details and keeps the editable hotbar beneath the library. Inventory retains its character preview, gear slots, bags and item actions within the updated frame.

The Adventure Board groups live adventure choices beside their details, with noticeboard contracts below. Chat uses larger readable text and the new frame while retaining channels, drafts and its mobile Back control.

title: Raid recovery, clearer mobile controls and referral tiers
summary: Raids can continue through disconnects, mobile combat leaves more room to see, and referral rewards show the active fee schedule.
changes: A raid can begin once ten living level-60 adventurers are ready, without choosing roles or meeting a tank/healer quota. Extra online members do not all need to be ready; they join and count toward the starting difficulty. Offline invitees are left out at the first start. The leader can appoint a co-leader to invite or remove members, and leadership passes to an online co-leader or member when the leader disconnects.

Offline members no longer block cleared-room gates or checkpoint retries. The remaining group can retry below ten players while retaining the starting difficulty and completion clock. Members can leave or be removed at cleared checkpoints and after wipes; reconnecting during combat preserves their health and position.

The mobile hotbar shows four skills at a time across four pages, preserving all sixteen saved assignments. Raid information is more compact, with a collapsible roster and visible personal mechanic warnings. The bottom menu keeps its icons and labels inside their buttons. Selected combat targets clear when they die, become invisible or leave targeting range, and friendly characters overlapping a monster no longer block selecting that monster.

The referral panel shows the active reward schedule, current tier and progress. Referral entry accepts either a code or a copied invite link. On the new tiered settlement, 1, 10, 25, 50 and 100 qualified referrals unlock 0.10%, 0.25%, 0.50%, 0.75% and 1.00% of their later MOSS Auction House purchase volume. The Wayfinder Sprite and Wayfarer Stag still unlock at ten and twenty-five.

The new settlement keeps the total auction fee at 5%, with 1.25% each for treasury and developer. Referral rewards come from the remaining 2.50% burn share. Earlier contracts retain their original fee schedule, referral terms and withdrawals; purchase reviews show the applicable split. New rates become available only when the new settlement is activated.

title: Keep your auctions open when linking a wallet
summary: Unsold listings automatically move to your verified wallet without cancellation or relisting.
changes: Verifying a linked wallet automatically moves your character’s unsold MOSS and ETH listings to it. Items, quantities, prices and listing IDs stay the same; no cancellation or relisting is needed. New listings and purchases also use that wallet.

Reserved auction payments and pending store or NFT orders keep their wallet protections until they finish. Signed payments and proceeds already earned retain their original wallet. My auctions explains the automatic migration.

title: Invite friends to Mossvale
summary: This release enables Auction House referrals, fee rewards and exclusive companion unlocks through the updated settlement contract.
changes: The activation release enables invite links and progress tracking in Referrals from the game menu. The panel shows whether the program is available on your realm. Each new referred account must reach level 20, play on two different UTC dates and spend at least $10 worth of MOSS on finalized Auction House purchases. All three requirements must be met; PvP spending is excluded.

One qualified referral unlocks 5% of the burn portion of fees from your qualified referrals’ future Auction House purchases. At 50, the share increases to 10%. The updated settlement credits rewards without changing the buyer price or seller proceeds. Collect them through Collect MOSS. Existing pending payments keep their signed terms, and balances from both older MOSS contracts remain separately collectible.

Ten qualified referrals unlock the exclusive Wayfinder Sprite, with ornate compass wings and a glowing lantern. Twenty-five unlock the Wayfarer Stag, with branching antlers, travel gear and two detailed saddles. Both have new models and portraits. Invite a nearby friend onto the account-bound stag; they accept and can leave at any time.

title: Longer PvP fights
summary: Player-versus-player damage is reduced by 80% to give fighters more time to react.
changes: Private arenas, friendly duels and the public colosseum now reduce damage between players and combat companions by 80% after defense. This includes basic attacks, spells, damage over time, pet attacks and reflected damage.
Eagle’s Eye, Power Shot, Venom Arrow and Viper Strike instead receive 90% PvP damage reduction, including their poison ticks. Venom Detonation keeps the extra reduction when consuming those poisons.
Hits deal at least 1 damage before shields. PvE damage, healing, shield strength and arena stun rules are unchanged.

title: Smoother Auction House purchases
summary: Pending purchases appear in your bags while payment confirms, and the market stays available to browse.
changes: The Auction House checks your linked wallet's MOSS balance before enabling Buy and checks again before reserving the listing. An unavailable balance check keeps the purchase disabled while other market actions remain usable.
After adding MOSS, choose Refresh market to check your balance again.

Pending purchases appear separately in your bags and in the Auction House Purchases tab. They cannot be used, learned, minted, traded or sold until payment is confirmed. You can keep browsing and open your bags while payment is pending.
Listings awaiting payment leave the public Browse and Exchange results. Pending items survive reconnects; an expired payment window still waits for verified payment or unpaid expiry before clearing.
Successful payments are checked promptly, reducing an avoidable delay before delivery.

title: Realm stability and accurate ping readings
summary: Safer reconnects during voucher checks and more accurate timing for the ping display.
changes: Leaving, reconnecting or changing tabs during an action now waits for that action to finish without treating an ordinary refusal as a realm storage failure.
A failed voucher eligibility check still keeps the voucher and daily allowance. Genuine save failures continue to stop the realm to protect player progress.
Ping now starts timing when its request is sent, excluding browser delay before the request. This corrects inflated readings on busy frames; it does not change network speed.

title: Auction House prepares Mossvale Wallet automatically
summary: Opening the Auction House gets your Mossvale Wallet ready for MOSS trading without a separate wallet button.
changes: Opening the Auction House or choosing Refresh market prepares your Mossvale Wallet and requests an ownership approval only if its address is not already linked to your character.
If you decline or wallet setup fails, background market updates will not repeat the prompt. Choose Refresh market or reopen the Auction House when ready to retry.
Active wallet listings, reserved payments, store orders and NFT claims must still be finished before changing your linked wallet. Every purchase still needs your approval.

title: Recover old auction proceeds with another wallet
summary: Old auction recovery helps you choose a wallet that supports Robinhood Chain.
changes: Settings → Wallet → Recover old auction proceeds opens the wallet picker and asks your selected wallet to switch to Robinhood Chain, adding the network when supported.

If the wallet cannot switch, the picker opens again. Choose a compatible wallet using the same address that received your original sales. Withdrawals return to that address and use its ETH for network fees.

title: New wild companions and Common pickup
summary: Eight new wild pets have a 0.025% drop chance, and pets can now pick up Common loot.
changes: Bramble Badger, Duskwind Raven, Ember Axolotl, Geode Hedgehog, Clover Mouse, Dewbell Dragonfly, Snowcap Stoat and Suncrest Peacock replace the previous wild-drop lineup with new Blender models and matching portraits. Each has a 0.025% chance (1 in 4,000) per eligible kill. Suncrest Peacock is exclusive to the level 40 Ashen Crown Titan world boss.

Fern Lynx, Moonveil Gryphlet, Cinder Salamander, Amethyst Terrapin, Blossom Jackalope, Lantern Sprite, Rime Red Panda and Crown Pangolin no longer drop. All existing learned pets, wallet-owned pets, summons and unlearned copies remain valid, including the original retired lineup. Existing NFT species numbers are preserved; the new species append to the expanded collection.

In Pets → Minimum item rarity, choose Common and better to include Common loot in automatic pickup. The choice is saved for your character. Uncommon remains the default, gold is always collected, and items that do not fit stay available for manual collection.

title: Safer Brave wallet sign-in
summary: Wallet sign-in opens a normal browser tab to avoid a Brave crash with MetaMask.
changes: Google, Apple and wallet sign-in open a separate browser tab while the game stays open. This avoids the popup-window crash triggered by MetaMask’s sidebar in Brave.
Reconnect game session also opens a normal browser tab. Sign-in still returns you to the game, and Continue in this tab remains available when the browser blocks a new sign-in tab.

title: The road to the Horned Apostle
summary: Six void chambers and Morgrath now lead into the Apostle raid.
changes: Clear 24 distinct creatures across the Void Garden, Umbral Kennels, Hollow Hive, Silent Ossuary, Black Forge and Fallen Citadel. Each creature has a detailed Blender model and its own special ability, with visible windups, strikes, spell releases and recovery poses.

Morgrath’s repaired rig keeps his sword, horns and armor attached through each attack, with distinct Cleave, Rift and Rupture animations. Fight him in his throne court. Avoid his sword cleave and void lane, enter the safe center of Rupture, and defeat the two Grave Knights he summons at half health.

Each cleared chamber opens its north gate. The leader rallies and restores the party before advancing. Wipes restart the current room, preserving cleared rooms and the original roster, roles and difficulty for this raid session.

Layered stonework, carved ruins, roots, chitin, ossuary reliefs, forge props and a shattered throne give the seven approach rooms distinct void silhouettes. Creature spells use Blender motifs, particles, glow and shape-matched impact effects; essential boundaries remain visible with Effects Off.
The full-route timer continues through the approach and retries. Personal raid rewards are awarded only after the Apostle falls.

title: MOSS wagers in 1v1 arenas
summary: Optional equal MOSS stakes for direct 1v1 challenges, with a 5% tax on the combined pot.
changes: Set a MOSS stake per player in the browser Arena finder. Both fighters review and accept the same stake, pot, tax and winner payout, then approve funding in the integrated Mossvale Wallet before entering. Arena screens keep the amounts and actions together with less helper text. Entry uses verified deposits in the current chain state (soft confirmation) without waiting for finality. A rare chain reorganization can cancel a match and leave remaining deposits refundable; recovery records are kept until finalized.
A 100-MOSS stake from each player pays the winner 190 MOSS, including their own stake. The 10-MOSS tax burns 8 MOSS and sends 1 MOSS each to the treasury and developer. Network fees are separate.

Forfeits and disconnects after entry, including countdown, lose the stake. Draws and cancelled entries return funded stakes without tax. Open MOSS wagers & payouts for saved results and refunds. Winners must collect before the displayed final refund deadline, currently one hour after accepted terms; afterward both stakes become refundable.

Rated matchmaking, 2v2, 3v3 and ordinary duels stay free. Gold is unchanged. MOSS wagering requires a configured, verified arena contract and is unavailable in native apps; this code update does not deploy the contract.

title: Class movement spells and Cleric Edicts
summary: Updated talent paths, three movement spells and Cleric Edict combinations follow the latest class designs.
changes: Rangers learn a twelve-meter Roll at level 9. Mages learn a fifteen-meter Blink at level 11 that removes slows. Clerics learn Lighspeed at level 9 to remove slows and move 50% faster for five seconds. Roll and Blink stop at obstacles.
Cleric healing, shielding and damage can now mark targets with Edicts of Light, Protection and Harm. Bouncing, Blanket and Renewable Edicts add bounded chains, weaker spread and reapplication.
New talent abilities add Edict of the Dawn’s healing over time and reactive pulses, Titan’s Edict’s reflecting shield, and Eternal Edict’s eight-second window of repeated activations.

Talent positions, prerequisites and branch requirements match the revised designs. Existing builds that remain valid are kept; previously valid builds affected by stricter requirements receive their points back.

Roll, Blink, Lighspeed, Poison Cloud and the three active Edicts have distinct Blender-made spell effects with moving leaves, portal fragments, wings, fungal blooms, solar pages, shield plates and hourglass rings. Thirteen detailed rendered icons cover those abilities and the six passive Edict talents, including the offline workshops.
Utility tooltips describe movement and Edict functions. Low effects retain recognizable spell forms while Off preserves essential combat cues.

title: Rated Solo, 2v2 and 3v3 arena
summary: Queue from anywhere, climb separate arena ranks and fight with reduced damage and chained-stun protection.
changes: The Arena finder now offers rated Solo (1v1), 2v2 and 3v3. Team leaders queue a preformed party of exactly two or three. Everyone accepts before entering, and no arena-entrance visit is required.

Each bracket starts at 1,000 MMR with saved win, loss and draw records. Matchmaking uses team average MMR, with a wider search over time. Climb Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond and Master; results show your rating change. Forfeits and disconnects count as team losses.

Private arena damage is reduced by 50%, including damage over time and companions. Stuns are 20% shorter, with chained stuns using 100%, 75%, 50%, 25% and then 0% duration. Immune appears above the target at 0%. The chain resets 15 seconds after the last successful stun ends.
Direct 1v1, 2v2 and 3v3 challenges are unrated practice matches and can start away from the entrance. Ordinary duels and public-ring PvP keep their existing combat rules.

title: The Apostle’s void sanctum
summary: A fractured void sanctum and detailed Blender spell models bring the Horned Apostle raid into the abyss.
changes: Fight on an obsidian platform surrounded by fractured monoliths, floating shards and violet/cyan runes. The open combat floor, movement bounds and ability ranges remain unchanged.

The Apostle now uses distinct casting poses for claws, stars, palms, judgment, chains, wings, Black Sun, Soul Harvest, clones and phase transitions. Detailed Blender spell models add jointed spectral hands, fractured stars, torn claw blades, layered feathers, soul skulls and eclipse coronas, all following the actual spell timing.

Void sparks, luminous trails, impact shockwaves and inward soul spirals now animate around the spell models. Chains carry traveling energy, seals pulse as they charge, and portals radiate soft glow. Effects quality controls particles; Bloom controls the added glow.
Four Hands highlights its safe opening. Suit symbols appear during their judgment phase, and Soul Chains show linked rings. Essential combat cues stay visible at every effects quality.

title: Choose your advertising preference before signing in
summary: New browser visits ask for an explicit Allow or Decline choice before sign-in or character selection.
changes: Choose Allow X cookies or Decline X cookies to continue. Both choices let you play, and your saved choice is remembered.
Native apps and browsers requesting no tracking skip the prompt and keep tracking off. If your choice cannot be saved, play continues with tracking off for that visit.

title: Clearer advertising choice
summary: A larger advertising notice explains what opting in to X cookies means.
changes: The notice explains how visits help show and measure Mossvale ads, what information X receives, and how to change your choice.
Allow X cookies and Decline X cookies are equally visible. You can play either way, and your saved choice is kept.
The notice is available in English, Simplified Chinese and Indonesian.

title: Rarer equipment and updated pet drops
summary: Existing equipment drop chances are halved, and the eight established drop companions share a 0.05% chance.
changes: The eight established drop companions, including Crown Pangolin, now have a 0.05% chance per eligible kill (1 in 2,000). Source monsters and Crown Pangolin's level-40 world-boss requirement remain the same. The new Horned Apostle rewards use their own raid rules.

Equipment drop chances are reduced by 50% across existing monsters, world bosses, dungeon caches and completion rewards. Original-dungeon caches and completion rewards now have a 50% equipment chance. Themed-dungeon side caches, midpoint bosses and final completions have 20%, 27.5% and 35% chances respectively.
Gear rarity and item stats are unchanged. Each eligible source still rolls independently, so multiple equipment drops remain possible in one dungeon run.

title: The Horned Apostle raid
summary: A level-60 raid for 10–20 players brings coordinated phases, personal rewards and specialist progression.
changes: Form a raid, select roles and ready the group. The Horned Apostle brings Death Marks, Shadow Crystals, clones, Four Suits, a split Death Realm and a final 90-second Death Counter. Reconnects retain raid state, and wipes allow another attempt.

Collect Apostle’s Souls, raid wings, a Death Apostle pet, Death Horns, Black Aura, a weapon skin, Sigils, Evolution Cores and the Death Defier title. Equip cosmetics and evolve your pet in Raid collection.

Raid clear rewards spin and stop on your saved prizes. Detailed Blender models bring carved Apostle armor, runes, layered wings and ornate encounter objects; attack boundaries retain the existing targeting and range system without the new red filled sight.

Claim a class specialist after Veilhaven or a raid clear at level 60. Earn separate job XP and upgrade to +15 using gameplay materials, with protection and repair items that preserve progression. The character cap remains 60.

Protection Rolls, Soul Revival Cores and Specialist Cases use reviewed MOSS-store purchases and can be traded for gold. Specialist NFT minting, activation, transfer and MOSS listings are available when the new collection contract is deployed and configured; this code update does not deploy that contract.

title: Moss Gates, clear times and dungeon leaderboards
summary: Varied chamber routes and full-clear results bring timed expeditions and per-dungeon rankings.
changes: Regional Moss Gates glow green. Large chambers vary in proportion and connect through one to three exits, with short side-room chains. Floor tiles stop at room edges so gaps remain clear. Combat exits stay sealed until the room is clear; sanctuary and wipe recovery remain available.

The timer starts when the first player leaves preparation for combat and continues through wipes. Defeat every combat room, including side chambers, to finish; killing the final boss alone does not grant completion rewards.

Full-clear results use Mossvale’s carved-wood frame, forest-green surfaces and rarity-bordered item slots, with time, monsters killed, wipes and four personal rewards: XP, the equipment roll, crystals and relics. The reward reels spin and stop one by one on your prizes, with an instant reveal for reduced motion. Claim items together or separately before leaving; rolls do not repeat, and full bags or failed saves keep items available.

Each dungeon has top-20 leaderboards for solo and parties of two, three or four across the public realms. Rankings require the original party throughout the timed run and exclude game-master assistance.

title: Optional advertising cookies
summary: Browser players can choose whether to share website visits with X for Mossvale advertising.
changes: X advertising stays off until you choose Allow. Decline to keep playing without the advertising tag.
Change your choice from the Privacy link on the sign-in screen or Account menu. Declining also stops the tag in other open tabs on the same website by reloading them.
The website tag is disabled in native apps and respects browser no-tracking signals.

title: Faster world startup
summary: Reduced the time needed to prepare the world when starting the game.
changes: The game prepares its existing terrain, towns and gathering spots more quickly.

title: Smoother dungeon travel and merchant sales
summary: Loot saves no longer hold up dungeon portals, and merchant sales can be queued.
changes: Dungeon room portals, rune seals, caches, entrances and exits remain usable while your manual or pet loot saves. Guardian, range and item ownership checks still apply.

Select your next merchant sale while earlier sales save. Pending rows leave the merchant list immediately; gold and inventory update only after the server confirms the sale. Failed or interrupted sales restore unconfirmed rows without automatically reselling them.

title: Buy MOSS auctions in one step
summary: One Buy confirmation covers your auction purchase.
changes: MOSS auction purchases show one Buy modal with the item and exact MOSS price. The token approval and purchase run together in one sponsored transaction; if either call reverts, both are rolled back.

Payments that fail before submission show the actual error and let you retry Buy instead of staying pending. An older unfinished wallet action shows a recovery instruction; uncertain submissions remain protected against duplicate payments.

title: More reliable MOSS payment checks
summary: Game servers use the configured Alchemy service for chain verification to avoid shared public RPC limits.
changes: Auction, store, voucher and NFT checks use the game's private Alchemy connection when configured. Pending payments keep their existing verification and duplicate-payment protections.

title: Smoother movement when updates arrive late
summary: Other players recover smoothly from delayed or uneven realm updates.
changes: Other players no longer keep stopping and jumping forward after connection latency increases. The client adjusts its short movement buffer and catches up gradually when delivery improves.
Fixed brief idle-animation flickers between movement updates. Players still stop at their last received position if updates stop; teleports and world transitions remain immediate.

title: Play in Bahasa Indonesia
summary: Indonesian joins English and Simplified Chinese in the game language selector.
changes: Choose Bahasa Indonesia before signing in, during character selection or in Settings → Language for translated interface text and game content.
Indonesian browser language preferences are detected automatically when no language is saved. Your choice stays on this device, and switching languages keeps you connected.
Player names and chat stay as written. Text without a translation continues to use English.

title: Fight around dungeon pillars
summary: Dungeon foes can pursue you around pillars, and an unreachable selected monster no longer blocks spells against nearby foes.
changes: Dungeon enemies route around pillars and other obstacles while chasing you, keeping their normal movement speed and respecting walls and closed gates.
Targeted offensive spells keep your selected monster when it is within range and has a clear path. Otherwise they choose the nearest reachable monster within spell range.
Tame Beast and explicitly selected opposing players or companions keep their chosen target.

title: Smaller bags and simpler auction purchases
summary: Compact inventory windows show your MOSS beside gold, and auction purchases keep a focused item-and-price approval.
changes: Desktop character inventory and bag overview windows use about 70% of their previous maximum width and height. Item lists still scroll, and phone controls retain their touch targets.
Both bag views show the primary Mossvale Wallet MOSS balance beside gold. The balance refreshes while bags are open; an unavailable balance is shown as a dash instead of zero.

Removed the auction payment-status and unpaid-purchase recovery buttons and instructions. Buy opens the item-and-MOSS approval; pending purchases are checked automatically without sending another payment.
Wallet transfers distinguish insufficient MOSS from missing ETH for the network fee. Manual transfers continue to use the player’s ETH.

title: Use purchases as soon as payment is processed
summary: Verified successful transactions no longer wait for Ethereum finality before delivering game rewards.
changes: Auction items, Gold Exchange lots, store rewards and voucher claims complete when the game verifies successful processing on the current canonical chain. Purchased items can be used or traded immediately after delivery.

Pet and mount mints, NFT transfers and house-deed ownership become available after current ownership is verified. A submitted transaction hash, failed transaction or unverified receipt does not grant a reward.
Completed off-chain rewards remain saved if the chain later reverses their payment; Mossvale accepts that settlement risk. NFT access continues to follow verified current ownership.
Unpaid expiry, retry safeguards, pricing and treasury funding still use finalized proofs to prevent duplicate claims and premature escrow release.

title: A clearer auction house with Mossvale Wallet
summary: Browse categories, compare listings and review your purchase beside the market. MOSS auctions use your built-in game wallet.
changes: Auction trading uses Mossvale Wallet directly, with no browser-wallet selector. The wallet reuses your game sign-in and renews an expired wallet session automatically when that sign-in is still valid.

The auction house now has category navigation, search above the listings, and an item-and-price panel beside the selected auction. Equipment also has class, rarity and minimum/maximum level filters, with rarity sorting and level requirements visible in the results. Phone layouts keep the same controls available.
Linking a wallet still requires a one-time ownership approval, and every payment requires your approval. New MOSS listings and purchases require the linked address to match your Mossvale Wallet.
Back up wallet now reveals only the primary wallet account’s private key in Turnkey’s secure export view, instead of a recovery phrase. The game does not receive the plaintext key.

Old balances, NFTs and signed purchases stay with their original wallet. Finish or cancel old commitments before switching. Settings → Wallet includes recovery for MOSS sale proceeds held by an old external wallet; these withdrawals use that wallet’s ETH.

title: A clearer statistics page
summary: Compact totals and a player chart up front make the statistics page easier to scan.
changes: Removed repeated subtitles and metric descriptions, with essential definitions available under About this data.

Seven-day and longer player charts retain measured averages during partial hours, including updates. All-time averages are weighted by the number of recorded samples. Dashed lines identify partial coverage; hours with no readings remain empty.
Unavailable and stale data remain labelled. Time ranges, chart inspection and CSV downloads remain available on desktop and mobile.

title: Fewer false disconnects after browser freezes
summary: The connection check gives delayed server replies time to arrive after a browser freeze before reconnecting.
changes: Long browser freezes and computer-clock changes no longer immediately trigger a reconnect before queued server replies can be processed. Connections that remain unresponsive still reconnect automatically.

title: Wallet fee sponsorship
summary: Mossvale Wallet uses your game login and pays eligible network fees directly within the game's limits, without depositing a withdrawable gas allowance.
changes: Fixed returning browsers keeping an older game version, missing Mossvale Wallet or repeatedly showing the update window; the normal game updater can recover without a hard refresh.
Fixed eligible wallet actions being rejected when sponsored gas is available.

Eligible purchases, sale withdrawals, voucher claims and pet NFT mints can have their network fees paid directly within the game's limits. No gas allowance is deposited into the player wallet or available to withdraw.

Players still approve each action and provide its purchase amount. Unsupported actions or unavailable sponsorship stop without automatically charging the player's ETH. Manual wallet transfers continue to use the player's own ETH.
Pending sponsored payments are tracked across retries; item delivery and payouts still require successful on-chain verification.
Wallet actions follow the selected realm. Returning to character selection or switching realms closes open wallet reviews; pending payments can be checked again after entering the game.

title: MEADGod and the Pons Lover title
summary: Meet MEADGod in Willowbrook and unlock Pons Lover through his one-time gold quest.
changes: MEADGod, a giant cottage spirit with a mossy roof and oversized glasses, now stands in Willowbrook, Greenwood.

Speak with MEADGod while nearby and out of combat, then pay exactly 100,000 gold to complete Pons Lover. The payment permanently unlocks the Pons Lover title for that character. Each character can complete the quest once.
Insufficient gold prevents payment. If saving fails, your gold and title ownership stay unchanged and you can retry in the dialogue.
Select Pons Lover from the title selector in Achievements after unlocking it. Your currently selected title stays unchanged until you choose another.

title: New character inventory and bag overview
summary: A refreshed inventory brings bag tabs, larger item grids and a separate overview to desktop and mobile.
changes: The character inventory places equipment and stats beside a combined item grid, with gold, capacity and tabs for individual equipped bags. In portrait, the character appears above the inventory.
Switch to the bag overview to see the backpack and each equipped bag in separate rows. Filter Equipment, Materials, Consumables, Quest or Misc, and sort each bag by Type, Name or Quantity.
Filtering and sorting keep saved item positions and bag contents unchanged. Choose All and Custom to rearrange slots. Existing item details, upgrades, equipping and bag management remain available.

title: Optional Mossvale Wallet
summary: Prepared an optional wallet using your Mossvale login, with inline management in Settings and game-funded network fees for eligible actions; it requires wallet and gas-funding setup before use.
changes: Choose Mossvale Wallet when available and continue with your existing game account to create or reopen your wallet. Your linked Mossvale wallet is used automatically, with no account selector. Linking and each transaction still require your approval. Existing browser wallet apps remain available.

For eligible auction purchases, sale withdrawals, voucher collection, pet NFT mints and MOSS store purchases, the game can top up the ETH shortfall for network fees within its limits; existing ETH counts toward those fees. You still supply the purchase amount and meet normal eligibility rules. Unavailable funding or unsupported actions stop without automatically spending your own ETH; external wallets keep their usual fee requirements.

Existing balances, NFT ownership and auction proceeds stay with their original wallet. Finish pending wallet purchases and listings before changing the linked address; saved voucher payouts must still be collected by their original recipient.

Settings → Wallet appears immediately below Graphics and opens your connected wallet directly to balances and controls inside Settings: view MOSS and ETH, copy a deposit address, send MOSS or ETH, view and transfer owned Mossvale NFTs, check pending transactions, and open explorer activity. Transfers show the recipient and maximum network fee before approval and use your own ETH. Back up wallet opens a separate recovery-phrase view. The optional wallet is unavailable in native wallet handoffs. Native MOSS auctions and NFT minting remain unavailable; mobile vouchers retain their existing external-wallet approval flow.
Wallet selection, sign-in, transaction review and backup dialogs use Mossvale’s timber frames, forest-green surfaces, brass buttons and cream text.

Where Mossvale Wallet is enabled, auction purchase reviews show the item, quantity and exact MOSS price; voucher approvals show the exact MOSS amount you will receive, and pet mint approvals show the pet’s image and name without unrelated item icons.

title: Clear the room to unlock its portals
summary: Every portal in a dungeon combat room stays sealed until all of that room’s monsters are defeated.
changes: Defeat every monster in your current chamber to unlock its outgoing portals, including the return portal. This also applies to optional side rooms.
Leaving or removing a living party member cannot be used to escape an uncleared combat chamber.
Forward portals still require their listed encounters and rune seals. The protected arrival sanctuary’s first room portal remains available immediately.

title: Larger dungeon rooms, portals and spike traps
summary: Dungeons now have larger enclosed chambers connected by real teleport portals, richer themed details and timed spike beds. The world view follows your current room.
changes: All seven dungeons receive larger, fully enclosed combat chambers with checkered stone floors, framed walls and glowing lanterns. Their themed encounters, rune seals, checkpoints and rewards remain.

All seven dungeons gain distinct architectural details: Rootvault root carvings and leaf clasps, Cindercrypt bronze grates and ember panels, Frosthollow ice crowns and silver runes, Nightroot thorn roots and crescent wards, Plagueworks specimen shelves and pipe valves, Emberfall furnace ribs and molten channels, and Veilhaven gold crests, amber lanterns and carved bell shrines.

Rootvault, Cindercrypt, Frosthollow and Nightroot receive eight distinct models for their sanctuary encounter leaders and final bosses, each with idle, walking, basic attack, special attack and death animations.
Only your current chamber and its occupants appear in the world view. Teleports, backtracking and checkpoint returns switch the visible room; the dungeon map retains its full layout.

Room teleports have stepped stone rings, glowing rims and blue vortices that look recessed into the floor. Locked portals hold floating chains and locks inside translucent blue domes until they unlock.

Use Interact (E by default) beside a floor portal to teleport between rooms. Forward portals require their listed encounters and rune seals; return portals allow backtracking. Clearing a main room opens its optional side chambers.
Every dungeon now starts in a protected arrival sanctuary, with a portal into the first combat room. Room arrivals leave clear space around portals and spike beds.

Fixed spike beds cycle through four seconds retracted, a 1.6-second warning and 2.4 seconds raised. Follow the clear center aisles or cross while the spikes are down; nearby beds can be at different points in their cycle.

Raised spikes can hit adventurers and combat companions once per bed per cycle, starting at 12% of maximum health before defense and shields. Entry, checkpoint and interaction spaces stay clear. Completing a run retracts its traps, and dream visits have no active spike traps.

title: Dungeon stability
summary: Fixed a server crash during companion combat in dungeons.
changes: Dungeon attacks targeting a Hunter companion no longer cause a server crash that disconnects players across the realm.

title: Bot security update
summary: Improved protection against automated play.
changes: Updated bot security.

title: Smaller game downloads
summary: Game updates reuse saved files and compress downloads to reduce data usage.
changes: Returning browsers reuse unchanged models and other saved game files instead of downloading the whole game again for each update.
New and changed game files download with lossless compression when supported. Saved files also load directly during play instead of being downloaded again.
An interrupted update keeps the previous complete version available. First visits and cleared browser storage still require downloading the game files.

title: Arrive in a fully drawn world
summary: A loading screen covers instance transitions while your destination is prepared.
changes: Entering a dungeon, dream or private arena, and returning outdoors, now shows a loading screen until the destination scenery, characters and first rendered view are ready.
Movement and gameplay controls stay paused during the transition. If an area cannot load, Reload world lets you try again.

title: Pick up loot without waiting
summary: Collect consecutive drops immediately while earlier pickups finish saving in the background.
changes: Collect another corpse or its remaining items without waiting for the previous pickup or your pet to finish saving. Pending loot appears in your bags immediately, and you can keep moving and fighting.
Pickups accepted while you are beside the corpse keep saving after you move away. New items become usable once their save succeeds; failed pickups leave the uncollected loot available.
Bags are full remains the only loot error popup. Other loot collection errors appear in System chat.

title: Less waiting between loot pickups
summary: Reduced background synchronization delays that affect loot collection, especially on Asia.
changes: Movement and health saves no longer trigger unnecessary refreshes on other realms, and remaining refreshes require fewer database round trips.
Loot and gold still become usable only after a successful save. Full-bag warnings remain unchanged.

title: Collectible mount drops and mount NFTs
summary: Keep extra mount drops to trade, and optionally mint eligible mounts in a separate Mossvale Mounts collection when enabled.
changes: Verdant Revenant keeps its 1 in 10,000 personal drop chance from the final Veiled Abbess encounter. Successful rolls now leave a mount item in personal loot, including for players who already own the mount.
Collect and learn a mount item, trade it, or list extra copies on the auction house. Mount items require bag space and cannot be sold to NPC merchants.

When the separate Mossvale Mounts NFT collection is enabled, eligible carried mount items and learned mounts can be converted into wallet-owned NFTs. Riding level and training are still required; transferring the NFT transfers its mount access.
Embermane and Cinderfang keep their store source. Finalized MOSS purchases can be converted when mount minting is enabled; refundable native-store purchases remain character-bound.
Briar Horse and Moonfang Wolf remain gold-vendor unlocks and cannot be minted.

title: MOSS voucher rewards and wallet minimum
summary: New voucher redemptions award $2–$10 and require at least $30 USD worth of MOSS in the linked wallet.
changes: New redemptions have a 90% chance of $2–$5 and a 10% chance of $6–$10 USD worth of MOSS. Each cent amount within a range is equally likely.

The linked wallet must hold at least $30 USD worth of MOSS before a new redemption. This balance is checked without spending or burning MOSS. Failed checks keep your voucher and daily redemption available.
Previously saved payouts keep their assigned rewards and remain available to refresh, collect or check without the new minimum. The one-redemption-per-account daily limit still resets at 00:00 UTC.

title: Reliable collection beside pets
summary: Manual loot collection waits for an ongoing pet pickup instead of rejecting the click.
changes: Collecting loot while your pet is saving a pickup now waits for that pickup to finish. Pets pause new pickups while your manual collection is waiting.
Full-bag warnings remain as popups. Other loot collection errors stay in System chat, and unsuccessful collection restores any pending loot display without a generic loot-save popup.

title: Mount collection preparation
summary: Prepares realm compatibility for collectible mount items and the separate mount NFT collection.
changes: Adds support for future mount items and saved mount NFT claims while preserving current mount rewards during the compatibility rollout.

title: Gear can drop again
summary: Owning a piece of gear no longer prevents another copy from dropping.
changes: Fixed gear rewards can drop even when another copy is equipped, carried, banked, auctioned or waiting to be collected.
Each drop is a separate item with the original name, stats, rarity and sale value. Keep it, sell it to a merchant, trade it or list it at auction.

title: Mobile startup recovery
summary: Prepared a native app fix for connections stuck on Opening the lantern roads...; it requires installing a new app build.
changes: A stalled startup connection shows a timeout and Reconnect after 15 seconds, even when the phone does not finish cancelling the request. Late results from an expired attempt cannot interrupt a newer connection.
The app retries every 15 seconds while active. Reconnect and returning to the app retry immediately.
This fix requires a new installed Android or iOS app binary. A game or wiki deployment does not update existing app binaries.

title: Steady mounted trading
summary: Fixed repeated rider jumps and camera shaking while buying or selling at NPC merchants on a mount.
changes: Standing still while a purchase or sale saves no longer causes repeated position resets.
Position corrections preserve the rider's saddle height and camera framing.

title: Keep fighting while loot saves
summary: Loot saves quietly in the background without interrupting skills and attacks.
changes: Skills, auto attacks and combat companions stay responsive while manual or pet loot pickups save.
Routine saving messages no longer interrupt loot collection. Failed saves still show an error and return any pending loot to its previous display.
A rejected auto-attack request no longer leaves the controls showing an attack that never started; you can retry without resetting the target or hotbar.
Collected items and gold still require save confirmation before they can be used, spent or traded. If saving fails, any remaining loot can be collected again.

title: Gear storage compatibility
summary: Prepare gear storage to retain separate copies of the same fixed equipment.
changes: Gear storage can retain individually identified copies through saves, upgrades, banks and auctions. Repeat fixed gear drops are enabled in a following release after all realms support these copies.

title: Realm and statistics stability
summary: Stalled connections no longer build an unlimited backlog of world updates, and live statistics recover more reliably.
changes: World updates catch up without retaining every outdated snapshot when a connection falls behind. A stalled connection can be disconnected before its backlog affects other players.
An abandoned statistics transaction can no longer keep all three realms' player counts frozen indefinitely.
A fresh realm count recorded while the statistics page loads stays available instead of briefly appearing offline.
Treasury totals use a working statistics-service RPC route while retaining fresh block, contract and finality verification.

title: Faster-feeling loot pickups
summary: See collected loot in your bags immediately while it saves.
changes: Manual loot pickups appear in your bags and disappear from the corpse immediately. Movement stays responsive while the pickup saves.
New loot becomes usable after confirmation. If saving fails, pending bag changes are reversed and remaining loot can be collected again.

title: Better investigation of missing loot
summary: Game masters can temporarily trace a character’s loot to investigate reported missing drops.
changes: Game masters can start and stop temporary loot diagnostics for a selected online character, then download a report of drop rolls, collection decisions, saving results and expired loot.
Tracing leaves loot chances and rewards unchanged.

title: MOSS auction tax
summary: This release activates a 5% seller tax on MOSS auction sales, split 80% to burning, 10% to the treasury and 10% to the dev team.
changes: The buyer pays the listed total. A 100 MOSS sale leaves 95 MOSS for the seller, burns 4 MOSS and sends 0.5 MOSS each to the treasury and dev team; ETH network fees remain separate.
Selling and purchase review show the auction tax split and seller proceeds. The tax also applies to MOSS paid for Gold Exchange lots, alongside the existing separate gold fee.

Open MOSS listings carry over without relisting, preserving their items, quantities and listed prices. Already-signed payments keep their original contract terms until paid or confirmed expired. Withdraw previous MOSS proceeds collects seller balances held by the original contract. Completed past sales are unchanged.

title: Class workshop rework and reliable hunter attacks
summary: The workshop class designs now drive new Knight talents, poison and fire spell changes, and hunter targeting.
changes: Knight talents add Wide Swing and Fine Cuts, a held Powerful Throw with shield recovery, Guard and Hold the Line, Adamant Guardian, Courageous Call and Into the Fray, and Lord of Battle. Changed Knight builds that no longer satisfy their prerequisites receive a free point refund.
The downloadable talent workshop starts with all 115 current talents and the updated Knight tree.
Knight trainers teach Charge at level 3 and Taunt at level 1. Taunt can choose an enemy attacking an ally when no target is chosen or the selected enemy already attacks you.

Rangers learn Poison Cloud at level 33. Starfall Arrow hits at most four enemies. Combined Assault requires a living companion already in melee range of its target. Mage Flamewave now leaves its authored burn.
